theories.label: Integrated Causal Reasoning / Contextually Flexible Causal Reasoning (ICR/CFCR)
theories.description: OpenEvo's own research position (Hanisch, Eirdosh, González Galli, Hartelt, Pérez & Cupo). Claims a scientifically complete evolutionary explanation must include organism agency as a real cause in cases where it's a documented contributor (e.g. niche selection, niche construction, behavioral plasticity) rather than relying on the decentralized Modern Synthesis mechanism alone. This project's own content -- the split between the 'Individuelle Entwicklung' and 'Evolutive Entwicklung' Basiskonzepte -- follows this position.
theories.evidentiary_maturity_note: The 2025 EvoFlex paper (linked below) found real empirical evidence that the agency/mentalism distinction this theory relies on is measurable and teachable -- not yet tested head-to-head against DCR-taught classroom outcomes specifically.

theories.label: Dichotomized Causal Reasoning (DCR)
theories.description: A rival position associated with researchers Kostas Kampourakis and Ross Nehm. Claims a complete evolutionary explanation should rely only on the decentralized Modern Synthesis mechanism (random heritable variation + differential reproduction); organism agency is deliberately excluded from the explanation to avoid reinforcing anthropomorphic misconceptions. Written here as OpenEvo's own characterization of Kampourakis's and Nehm's published position, for comparison -- not confirmed or reviewed by either of them. Shown here deliberately, not omitted: this project's researcher view is meant to show the real, live academic disagreement, not just the side it follows.
theories.evidentiary_maturity_note: Not rated -- this project doesn't hold this position, so rating its own evidentiary maturity isn't this project's call to make.

theories.evidentiary_maturity_note: Not rated -- unsourced placeholder, see description.

theories.label: Anthropomorphic Intentionality in Evolutionary Change (documented misconception, not a theory)
theories.description: Attributing conscious deliberation, awareness of future evolutionary consequences, and intentional planning toward an evolutionary outcome to a non-human organism. Example student statement: "Some ancestors of the cheetahs recognized that they could not catch enough prey. Hence, they trained to run faster." Both ICR and DCR agree this specific statement is a misconception -- their real disagreement is about a different, more subtle case (see the DCR/ICR relation below).

theories.label: Species Essentialism / Typological Thinking (documented misconception, not a theory)
theories.description: The belief that all members of a species share one fixed 'true nature,' and that variation between individuals is a deviation from that type rather than the raw material evolution works on. Example: "All cheetahs are built to run fast -- that's just what cheetahs are like."

theories.label: Agency as Binary: Humans Have It, Other Organisms Don't (documented misconception, not a theory)
theories.description: Treating agency as all-or-nothing -- crediting humans with goals and choices while categorically denying any non-human organism the same, sometimes inconsistently within the same student's own other answers. Found directly in the EvoFlex research: students who credited human behavior as an evolutionary cause chose that same option less often when the identical question was asked about a non-human case.

theories.label: Agency Negation: Correct Response vs. Novel Misconception (a live, concrete assessment dispute)
theories.description: The same real student response -- "organism behavior played no role in the evolution of this trait," for the classic cheetah-running-speed case -- is scored CORRECT by a real DCR-aligned assessment tool (KAEVO 2.0) and INCORRECT by a real ICR-aligned assessment tool (EvoFlex). This isn't a scoring bug in either tool. It's the direct, concrete consequence of the DCR/ICR disagreement above: both instruments cannot be correct at once for the same case. Not a theory itself -- a documented point of live disagreement between the two theories in this list.
